newsitem.title: USA: US cotton group sees more exports to Latin America.
newsitem.headline: US cotton group sees more exports to Latin America.

text.p: A group of U.S. cotton producers will meet textile manufacturers in Brazil, Colombia and Ecuador next week to find ways to boost U.S. cotton exports, National Cotton Council said Friday.
Latin America now buys 25 percent of U.S. raw cotton exports, purchasing about 1.2 million bales in 1996-97, the trade group said. In 1992, Latin America bought 200,000 bales of U.S. cotton.

"Latin America has become a significant market for U.S. cotton, and there is tremendous potential for continued exports there," said Fred Starrh, a cotton producer from Shafter, Calif, who will be part of the delegation.
Brazil is now the largest cotton importing country in the world, buying 2.6 million bales annually, the Cotton Council said.
The trade group's export promotions arm will triple its spending in Latin America in 1997-98 to try and increase demand for American cotton, the group said.
